analysis:
All changes are CI workflow hardening. They sit outside the provider runtime threat model: no provider, coordinator, attestation, key or cache-storage code changed, so A-001 to A-020, TB-002 to TB-014 and T-041 are unaffected.

What I examined:
1. A new 'Choose this job's Actions cache' step is added to ci-master.yml (release-integrity head 77-89, docs head 227-239), desktop.yml (frontend head 37-49), landing.yml (head 35-47), provider-release-cache.yml (head 81-93), and provider-tests.yml (patch excerpt only). On a Darkbloom runner with no DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL it writes CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off to GITHUB_ENV. The restore and save cache steps and setup-node's cache input are then gated on that variable (ci-master head 102, 143, 249, 290; desktop head 54; landing head 51). No attacker-controlled data reaches GITHUB_ENV, because only the constant string is written. This reduces the chance that a Darkbloom sandbox reaches GitHub's own Actions cache.
2. The 'Discard a damaged or unsafe cached .git' step (ci-master head 111-136 and 258-283) is a net hardening. It rejects a restored .git that is a symlink, holds symlinks, holds non-sample hooks, or whose config sets core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or an include, before any git command reads it. 'git config --file' only parses the file, so it does not execute anything.
3. Residual observation, not filed: the config check is a denylist. Other execution-capable keys such as filter.*.smudge/clean/process, core.sshCommand, credential.helper, core.pager and diff.external are not screened. Exploiting this needs a poisoned master-scoped cache entry first. SAVE_CACHES limits cache writes to master pushes, so PRs cannot write cache, and the new check is stricter than the base.
4. The unchanged actions/cache and actions/checkout SHA pins and the permissions: contents: read are preserved.
5. review-package in desktop.yml (head 68) still uses cache: npm unconditionally. It runs on a Blacksmith macOS runner, not a Darkbloom sandbox, so it is out of the new gating's scope.

Limits: the provider-tests.yml patch is only a truncated excerpt and its full head text was not supplied. I confirmed the same step pattern in its excerpt but could not check every changed range. The Darkbloom runner's cache endpoint (DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL) and the runner-name convention are external contracts that I did not verify.
